facts.raw_span: A 15-year-old boy with biopsy-proven Crohn disease
infiximab therapy (5 mg/kg subcutaneous injection every 8 weeks)
later switched to adalimumab (40-mg/0.8-mL subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks) due to disease relapse
Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Both lower eyelids were ectropic
Visual acuity was 20/20 OU
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable

concepts.why: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids and crusty plaques on the eyelid margins suggest blepharitis
Both lower eyelids were ectropic, indicating ectropion
Biopsy-proven Crohn disease and disease relapse suggest active Crohn disease
Presence of Crohn disease, blepharitis, and ectropion suggests an underlying autoimmune disorder
It explains the normal visual acuity despite significant eyelid and conjunctival findings.

rationales.F01: Biopsy-proven Crohn disease is a strong indicator for Crohn disease and a moderate indicator for autoimmune disorder.
rationales.F04: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids are a strong indicator for Blepharitis and a moderate indicator for Dry eye syndrome.
rationales.F05: Ectropic lower eyelids are a strong indicator for Ectropion.
rationales.F06: Normal visual acuity is a moderate rule-out for Dry eye syndrome.
rationales.F07: Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins are a strong indicator for Blepharitis and a moderate indicator for Dry eye syndrome.
rationales.F08: Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia is a strong indicator for Conjunctivitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids and crusty plaques on the eyelid margins strongly support Blepharitis, with Ectropion also present but less specific to the overall clinical picture.
